chunks: Sa'd, from Abū al-Jawzāʾ al-Munabbih ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUlwān al-Kalbī, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his fathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
"Ghusl (ritual bath) is due from seven things: from janabah, and it is obligatory; and from washing the dead, and if you purify yourself, it will suffice you." And he mentioned other than that.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: His statement, "and if you purify yourself, it will suffice you," is to be understood as taqiyyah, because we have explained the obligation of ghusl upon the one who has washed a dead person, and this agrees with the ʿAmmah, so it is not acted upon.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: it sufficed you; meaning it would fulfill the requirement
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation/precautionary conformity for protection in sensitive circumstances
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the broader Sunni majority, whose view is said here to align with the non-acted-upon wording
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required in specific states of ritual impurity
key_terms.تَطَهَّرْتَ: you purified yourself; here referring to an alternative purification expression in the report
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: washing the deceased; here, the act connected to a legal ruling of purification
key_terms.وُجُوبَ: obligation; legal necessity in jurisprudential usage

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl obligatory after washing a deceased person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses causes requiring ghusl (ritual bath), including janabah and washing a deceased person. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī states that the wording suggesting mere purification would suffice after washing the dead is interpreted as taqiyyah, and that the binding ruling is the obligation of ghusl in such a case.
